280	## 3. ROSTER COUNTING (B-1)
281	
282	### 3.1 What counts OPEN
283	
284	`payload/hooks/dispatch-preflight.sh:786-805`, `budget_roster_counts <roster file> -> "<open> <claimed>"`:
285	
286	- `:794` — only lines matching `roster-state/v1|status=intended|` are considered. **`status=intended`
287	  is the ONLY status that counts**; `confirmed` and `identified` rows are skipped outright.
288	- `:795-799` — dedupe by `name=`; first occurrence wins.
289	- `:791` + `:799` — a name is **closed** iff the file also holds a line beginning
290	  `landing-swept/v1|` whose text contains `|name=<that name>|`. Any marker state closes it —
291	  the check is on the name, not on `state=MET`.
292	- `:800` — everything else increments `open`.
293	- Called at `:839`; the refusal at `:847` prints `writers: budget=… open=… with-this-dispatch=…`.
294	
295	The row a dispatch writes is `dispatch-preflight.sh:1715` and it is `status=intended` with
296	`agent_id=` empty, so **every dispatch starts life counted OPEN and stays that way until a
297	`landing-swept/v1` line names it.**
298	
299	### 3.2 When a row is closed, and who writes the marker
300	
301	`SWEPT_SCHEMA="landing-swept/v1"` at `payload/hooks/landing-gate.sh:148`.
302	
303	**One writer, one line:** `landing-gate.sh:631-632`
304	
305	```
306	printf '%s|at=%s|session=%s|name=%s|agent_id=%s|state=%s\n' \
307	  "$SWEPT_SCHEMA" "$NOW" "$SID" "$NAME" "$AID" "$STATE" >> "$ROSTER_FILE"
308	```
309	
310	```
311	$ /usr/bin/grep -n "SWEPT_SCHEMA" payload/hooks/*.sh
312	payload/hooks/landing-gate.sh:148   payload/hooks/landing-gate.sh:452
313	payload/hooks/landing-gate.sh:562   payload/hooks/landing-gate.sh:632
314	```
315	
316	The gate's own comment at `:561-563` asserts the same single-writer fact.
317	
318	The path to that append (`landing-gate.sh:118-133`, `:177-183`, `:525-580`, `:588-632`):
319	
320	1. The Stop payload must have a `background_tasks` key at all (`:181`) — absent → `exit 0`.
321	2. `LIVE_IDS` is built from `background_tasks[].id` (`:183`). A candidate whose agent id is
322	   still in that list is skipped as in flight (`:590`).
323	3. **Teammates are skipped by the sweep arm entirely** (`:529-570`): a teammate is keyed in
324	   `background_tasks[]` under a namespace its `agent_id` is not in and *never leaves that
325	   array*, so the landed/live predicate would read every teammate as landed 2.8 s after
326	   dispatch. The sweep only ever **rechecks** a teammate row that already carries an `UNMET`
327	   marker, and only to supersede it with `MET` (`:552-570`, `:616-618`). A teammate row with
328	   **no marker at all is left exactly as it is, forever** (`:546-550`).
329	4. A row that "declares nothing" (`dl[nm] == ""`) is skipped as vacuously MET (`:574`) — and
330	   therefore **never gets a marker either**.
331	
332	**This is B-1's mechanism, in the code.** A `Deliverable-waiver:` researcher/critic/auditor is
333	dispatched as a teammate, delivers by message, is stopped by name, and never has a marker
334	written for it — so `budget_roster_counts` counts its `status=intended` row OPEN forever.
335	The two independent reasons it never gets one are the teammate skip at `:529` and the
336	declares-nothing skip at `:574`.
337	
338	### 3.3 `stop-orders.sh standdown` — computes the verdict, writes nothing
339	
340	`payload/hooks/stop-orders.sh:490-591`. It shells out to `session-sweeper.sh verdict`
341	(`:498-500`), folds the roster once (`:511`), and per verdict line (`:526-565`) classifies:
342	
343	```
344	:545  if [ "$(line_field "$_l" acked)" = "yes" ]; then _why="acked"
345	:547  elif [ "$_state" = "WAIVED" ];                  then _why="waived"
346	:549  elif [ "$_state" = "MET" ] && [ -n "$_deliv" ]; then _why="met"
347	```
348	
349	Rows with a `_why` go into the `STAND DOWN` list (`:553-556`); everything else into
350	`LEFT ALONE` (`:562-565`). The verb then prints and exits (`:571-590`), closing with
351	`"This script stopped nothing"` (`:588`).
352	
353	**Confirmed: `standdown` writes nothing to the roster.** The only appends in the file are in
354	the `order`/`give` arm at `:459` and `:461`, and they go to `$ORDERS_FILE`
355	(`stop-orders-<session>.state`), never to `roster-<session>.state`. It does have one side
356	effect: `worktree_land` on a discharged row's tree (`:555-560`), which is a git operation, not
357	a roster write. So B-1's "the verdict already exists; make it write" is accurate — the
358	`waived`/`met` branch at `:547-550` is the exact place a `landing-swept` append would go.
359	
360	### 3.4 `stop-guard.sh` on TaskStop — could it append?
361	
362	`stop-guard.sh` is the `PreToolUse|TaskStop` hook. It is a **read-and-refuse wall**: it
363	resolves the target, applies the ownership rule, and consumes `session-sweeper.sh verdict`
364	rather than forming its own opinion (`:696-703`). It appends nothing to the roster today —
365	`SWEPT_SCHEMA` does not appear in it (grep above), and its only writes are through
366	`state_paths` to the observation state file.
367	
368	Mechanically it *could* append the marker: by the time it decides, it holds `$AGENT_ID`
369	(`:539`), `$AGENT_NAME` (`:586`), `$SID`, `$STATE_DIR`, `$ROSTER_FILE` (`:588`) and the
370	sweeper's verdict line — the exact five fields `landing-gate.sh:631` writes. The design cost
371	is that it would make a **second writer** of a schema whose single-writer property is asserted
372	in `landing-gate.sh:561-563` and leaned on by the `magent[nm]` fallback at `:566-570`. Note
373	too that it fires on the *attempt* to stop, before the harness has stopped anything, and it
374	exits 2 on refusal — so an append placed before the refusal would mark rows closed for stops
375	that never happened.

379	## 4. STOP RESOLUTION (B-2)
380	
381	### 4.1 Enumeration, both sides
382	
383	`stop-guard.sh:95-110` `scan_subagent_dirs <typed> <dir>...`:
384	
385	```
386	for meta in "$sub"/agent-*.meta.json; do
387	  base="${meta##*/}"; base="${base%.meta.json}"; id="${base#agent-}"
388	  name=$(jq -r '.name // empty' "$meta")
389	  if [ "$id" = "$typed" ] || { [ -n "$name" ] && [ "$name" = "$typed" ]; }; then

399	  **plus** `adopted_subagent_dirs` (`:146-180`), which reads this session's roster for

406	### 4.2 MATCH_COUNT
407	
408	`stop-guard.sh:474-543`:
409	
410	```
411	:474  MATCHES=$(scan_subagent_dirs "${RAW%@*}" "$SUB" ${ADOPTED_DIRS+"${ADOPTED_DIRS[@]}"})
412	:480  MATCH_COUNT=0
413	:481  [ -n "$MATCHES" ] && MATCH_COUNT=$(printf '%s\n' "$MATCHES" | grep -c .)
414	:508  if [ "$MATCH_COUNT" -eq 0 ]; then   … deny "unresolved" (or PASSTHROUGH if not address-shaped)
415	:533  if [ "$MATCH_COUNT" -gt 1 ]; then   deny "ambiguous: N agents … Name the agent by its id"
416	:537  IFS='|' read -r AGENT_ID META SUBDIR <<< "$MATCHES"
417	```
418	
419	`stop-check.sh:479-511` mirrors it, but on ambiguity **prints every candidate with a
420	constructed `name@session-<id8>` stop address** (`:500-507`) and decides nothing (`:511`).
421	
422	**Two facts that together are B-2:**
423	
424	1. **`:474` strips the `@…` suffix before scanning** (`${RAW%@*}`). So `w1-rc`,
425	   `w1-rc@session-305130fb` and `w1-rc@session-anything` all produce the *same* MATCH_COUNT.
426	2. **The ambiguity deny at `:533` runs BEFORE `typed_is_identity`** (defined `:645-658`, first
427	   called `:686`). So the qualified form cannot rescue an ambiguous name: the guard refuses at
428	   `:534` and never reaches the clause that would have accepted the launcher-qualified
429	   spelling.

457	**The nested shape has no `name` field at all** (9 of the 40 sampled). `scan_subagent_dirs`
458	matches on `id` or `.name`, so those agents are addressable by id only — worth knowing before

469	$ ls */subagents/*.meta.json | sed 's|.*/subagents/||' | sort | uniq -d

476	
477	Both files are byte-identical (293 bytes, same JSON above), the two transcripts
478	`agent-aw1-rc-e0886335875ba2d1.jsonl` exist in both directories, and the `teamName` names a
479	**third** session, `305130fb-3c86-42bf-8b57-768781abb2b8`, whose own `.jsonl` is on disk but
480	which has **no `subagents/` directory**. Mtimes differ by 31 minutes — so "prefer the newest
481	`meta.json`" is a workable dedupe tiebreak here, and the file contents are identical anyway.
482	
483	This is the exact fixture B-2 needs: **one agent id, one name, two session directories.**
484	If both directories are in scope (this session's own plus an `adopted_from` row naming the
485	other), `scan_subagent_dirs` emits two lines and `MATCH_COUNT=2` → the deny at `:534`.

487	### 4.5 How `name@session-<launcher>` is parsed
488	
489	`stop-guard.sh:645-658`:
490	
491	```
492	typed_is_identity() {
493	  [ "$RAW" = "$AGENT_ID" ] && return 0
494	  case "$RAW" in *@*) : ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
495	  [ -n "$ROSTER_TEAMMATE" ] && [ "$RAW" = "$ROSTER_TEAMMATE" ] && return 0
496	  local base="${RAW%@*}" suffix="${RAW##*@}" want
497	  [ "$base" = "$AGENT_ID" ] || { [ -n "$AGENT_NAME" ] && [ "$base" = "$AGENT_NAME" ]; } || return 1
498	  case "$suffix" in session-*) : ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
499	  want="${suffix#session-}"
500	  [ -n "$want" ] || return 1
501	  case "$OWNING_SID" in "$want"*) return 0 ;; esac      # PREFIX match on the OWNING dir
502	  return 1
503	}
504	```
505	
506	`OWNING_SID` is derived from the directory the winning meta was found in (`:587`), and
507	`ROSTER_TEAMMATE` from the roster row's `teammate_id=` field (`:632`). The constructed fallback
508	address is `"${AGENT_NAME:-$AGENT_ID}@session-$(… OWNING_SID | cut -c1-8)"` (`:637`).
509	
510	`typed_is_identity` is consulted **only** inside the foreign-owner branch
511	(`:660-686`: `if [ "$OWNING_SID" != "$SID" ] && [ -z "$ROSTER_ID_MATCH" ]`). It is unreachable
512	when `MATCH_COUNT > 1`. Ownership by id is established at `:594-618` from a roster row with
513	status `confirmed` **or** `identified` and a non-empty `agent_id` — never `intended` (`:600-606`).
514	
515	`is_address_shaped` (`:500-506`) is the separate carve that decides whether a `MATCH_COUNT=0`
516	target is refused or passed through; it accepts `*@session-*`, `^a[0-9a-f]+$`, and
517	`^a.+-[0-9a-f]{16}$`.

524	
525	`active_plan` at `payload/scripts/lib/run.sh:93-122`; `open_runs` at `:268-330`.

545	### 5.2 Three canonicalizers of "a plan path for comparison" (D2)
546	
547	| # | site | code | behaviour on a relative path | on a trailing slash |
548	|---|---|---|---|---|
549	| 1 | `payload/scripts/lib/binding.sh:56-67` `_bind_resolve` | `case "$p" in /*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac`, then `dirname`/`basename`, `cd … && pwd -P` | **refuses (rc 1)** | `dirname`/`basename` strip it: `a/b/` → `<abs a>/b` |
550	| 2 | `payload/hooks/session-poker.sh:1475-1484` `adopt_plan_key` | `${1%/*}` / `${1##*/}`, `cd … && pwd -P`, **falls back to the raw string** on failure; a path with no `/` returns unchanged | **resolves against the CALLER'S cwd** | `a/b/` → d=`a/b`, b=`""` → `<abs a/b>/` |
551	| 3 | `payload/hooks/session-poker.sh:2058-2059` `BIND_DIR_REAL` | `BIND_DIR="${BIND_PATH%/*}"; BIND_DIR_REAL="$(cd "$BIND_DIR" && pwd -P)" && BIND_REAL="$BIND_DIR_REAL/${BIND_PATH##*/}"` | resolves against cwd; on failure `BIND_REAL` stays **empty** | same split as #2 |

557	stores the **canonical** spelling (`value="$want"`, `:126`), which is why the divergence is
